modifications: Entries were selected, normalised (HTML removed, years parsed, headline titles shortened to about 100 characters with an ellipsis), merged and de-duplicated across sources, ranked, capped per day and category, and sorted. Summaries keep the source wording. did_you_know facts are either Wikipedia "Did you know" hooks (text only, reformatted) or one-sentence rewordings of existing entries (prefixed with the date, possibly shortened). Image links are unmodified Wikimedia URLs.

did_you_know.fact: On August 14, 1933: Loggers cause a forest fire in the Coast Range of Oregon, later known as the first forest fire of the Tillamook Burn; destroying 240,000 acres (970 km2) of land.
On August 14, 1893: France becomes the first country to introduce motor vehicle registration.
August 14 is observed as Falklands Day is the celebration of the first sighting of the Falkland Islands by John Davis in 1592.
On August 14, 1901: The first claimed powered flight, by Gustave Whitehead in his Number 21.
August 14 is observed as Partition Horrors Remembrance Day commemorates the victims and sufferings of people during the Partition of India in 1947.
